purpose: Add bounded cooperative intrachain collapse while preserving the linear model's high-contact behavior and Rg plateau.

variables.m_intra: Raw nonbonded intrachain contact count for one chain.
variables.N: Number of beads in the chain.
variables.q: (m_intra - m_ref) / N, an intensive shifted contact density.
variables.m_ref: Reference contact count used only to center q; default 0 unless the fitter already uses another reference.

reduced_potential_per_chain.cooperativity: A(T) = A0 initially; optionally A(T) = h_A/T - s_A if validation supports temperature dependence.
reduced_potential_per_chain.saturation_parameter: q_sat > 0 controls where the nonlinear attraction stops strengthening.

behavior.low_to_moderate_q: Approximately b(T)q - A(T)q^2 + A(T)q^4/q_sat^2, giving negative-quadratic cooperativity plus positive-quartic stabilization.
behavior.high_q: The cooperative correction approaches the constant -A(T)q_sat^2, so the marginal slope returns to the linear bias b(T) instead of becoming increasingly attractive.
behavior.expected_effect: Sharper collapse than the linear model without the continued overcollapse caused by an unchecked negative m^2 term.

multichain_rule.requirement: Evaluate the saturating intrachain term separately for each chain using that chain's own m_intra_alpha.
multichain_rule.warning: Do not apply the nonlinear function to total contacts or to m_intra + m_inter, because that creates artificial cross-chain coupling.

implementation_notes: Use raw lattice contact counts; never apply the molecular-to-lattice contact offset inside the Hamiltonian.
Update the energy from old and new per-chain intrachain contact counts during Monte Carlo moves.
Keep interchain contacts linear in the first implementation.
Fit against both P(m|T) and P(Rg|T), and compare against the existing linear, quadratic, and quartic models using held-out temperatures.
Enforce q_sat > 0 and preferably A(T) >= 0 over the fitted temperature range.

initial_parameterization.optional_extension: Add h_A and s_A only if cross-validation shows a clear improvement.
